messages:
sre-qa: FYI seeing a big P99 regression for streaming responses after today's API rollout. p50 ~ unchanged, p99 ~3x. Happening across a few small customers.
ryan: ugh. which endpoint? any correlation with model or route?
sre-qa: primarily eventsource /v1/chat/stream and some tool-call flows. traces attached: https://redwood-traces/trace/abc123
anya: I ran a quick flamegraph on a replay of a failing trace — looks like serialization time jumps and a lot of time in kernel selection path + KV prefetch.
sam: can you paste the flame snippet? curious if it's a blocking syscall or pure CPU.
anya: paste: ```diff
--- master
+++ deploy-2025-06-04
@@
- kernel_autoselect()  5ms
+ kernel_autoselect()  18ms
- kv_prefetch()  2ms
+ kv_prefetch()  12ms
- serialize_frame() 1ms
+ serialize_frame() 10ms
```
ryan: interesting — kernel_autoselect ballooned. any recent PRs touching runtime autoselect or protocol framing?
sam: IIRC the merge today added an early compatibility check in the API layer that does a small dry-run of tool-call serialization to validate schema. Could that be triggering repeated prefetches?
perf-bot: ci/perf-smoke failed on eventstream latency test in canary: delta p99 +220% (run id 8942). Full logs: https://ci/8942/logs
sre-qa: also noticed a pattern: under steady small requests, we see many short-lived kernel selections per request instead of one. suggests cache key mismatch.
anya: that's consistent with a change that invalidates per-request kernel cache or appends a non-deterministic header to proto, altering fingerprint.
ryan: bisect plan: revert the API dry-run PR in canary and re-run perf-smoke. If regression goes away -> root cause. If not, dig deeper.
sam: I can push a revert to canary in 10min and kick perf job.
deploy-bot: revert PR #4821 deployed to canary at 2025-06-04T16:12:07Z (sha: def456).
perf-bot: perf-smoke re-run enqueued (8943).
perf-bot: perf-smoke results (8943): p99 delta -10% relative to canary baseline (regression disappeared).
anya: confirmed on a quick replay — kernel_autoselect and kv_prefetch times back to normal. serialize_frame also dropped.
ryan: ok root cause = API dry-run serialization check. Why does it affect kernel selection?
anya: theory: dry-run path was calling model->select_kernel() with a slightly different sequence length hint and temp KV prefetch, which triggers a new cache entry per request and prevents reuse of previously chosen kernels. That amplified serialization cost due to more frequent codec negotiation.
sam: from code review: dry-run created a short-lived proto wrapper that included a timestamp header to help debugging. that randomized the request fingerprint.
ryan: Oof. we need a hotfix: remove timestamp from fingerprinting and avoid calling select_kernel twice.
sre-qa: for now hold the rollout to prod and escalate to release. marking rollout-hold and opening a tracking ticket INF-2025-118.
deploy-bot: rollout status: hold applied to release 2025-06-04 (reason: streaming latency regression).
anya: I'll prepare a PR to fix the dry-run to use a non-fingerprinted path (skip cache-influencing headers) and add a regression test that runs perf-smoke during PR gating.
ryan: thanks — also add an assertion that select_kernel is idempotent in the same logical request.
sam: reprod steps written in INF-2025-118, attaching replay script and perf traces.
sre-qa: great, thanks team. keeping an eye on any other anomalies. :thumbsup:
